best_architecture: Recommended pattern: a layered 'parse once, query many' AST service with a polyglot core and language-specific edit backends. (1) PARSING LAYER — use tree-sitter as the universal parser. It produces a concrete syntax tree per file, is error-tolerant (returns a usable tree even on syntactically broken / in-progress code, which LSP-style tools and Semgrep cannot), supports incremental re-parsing of only the edited region (~36x faster than re-parsing in reported benchmarks), and has uniform grammars + an S-expression query language across Python/TypeScript/Rust/Go/etc. This is the single biggest design decision: one parser, one query dialect, all languages, so the agent never depends on the LLM to 'read' structure. (2) SYMBOL-MAP LAYER — run tree-sitter tag/scope queries (the standard `tags.scm` / `locals.scm` query files shipped per grammar) to extract definitions (functions, classes, methods, structs, traits) and references (calls, type uses, imports). Build a directed graph: edges go from each reference site to its definition site. This is the Aider 'repo map' architecture. Rank symbols by importance with PageRank over the symbol/file graph (a function called by 20 others is more valuable context than a private helper); personalize the ranking toward files currently in the agent's working set (Aider uses a ~50x multiplier for chat-referenced files). Pack the top-ranked signatures into an adaptive token budget so the LLM gets a concise, dependency-aware map instead of raw files. Emit the map as structured JSONL (name, kind, signature, parent, file:line) so it is both LLM-readable and machine-queryable. (3) STRUCTURAL SEARCH/EDIT LAYER — split read-only matching from semantic rewrites. For polyglot structural search-and-replace and lint-style rules, use ast-grep (Rust, multi-core, usable as a library, pattern + YAML rule + API interfaces) — ideal for cross-language pattern migrations and 'find every call shaped like X' queries. For security/taint and a large curated rule ecosystem, use Semgrep. For genuinely SEMANTIC TypeScript/JavaScript refactors that must follow the type system (rename a symbol and update every reference across files, move a symbol between files and fix imports, find references, strip path aliases), tree-sitter is NOT enough — use ts-morph (TypeScript Compiler API wrapper) because it has a real type checker and cross-file reference resolution; keep all edits in-memory and commit atomically. POLYGLOT STRATEGY: unified interface, pluggable backends. Expose one stable agent-facing API (e.g. get_symbols(file), find_references(symbol), rename(symbol), search(pattern), rewrite(pattern, replacement)) and route per language: tree-sitter for parsing/symbol-map everywhere; ast-grep/Semgrep for syntactic search-rewrite everywhere; ts-morph for type-aware TS/JS edits; LSP servers (or rope/jedi for Python, rust-analyzer for Rust) where true semantic rename is required. Do NOT try to force one tool to do everything — tree-sitter gives breadth and resilience, the language-specific backends give correctness for renames/moves. KEY DECISIONS THAT MATTER MOST: (a) prefer error-tolerant tree-sitter over compiler/LSP for the always-on symbol map so the agent works on broken code mid-edit; (b) separate 'structural match' (cheap, syntactic, polyglot via ast-grep) from 'semantic refactor' (expensive, type-aware, per-language via ts-morph/LSP); (c) cache parsed trees and incrementally update them keyed by file mtime/hash; (d) rank-and-budget the symbol map (PageRank + token budget) rather than dumping all symbols; (e) for any structural rewrite, manipulate the AST and re-print, never do text/regex replacement, to preserve correctness. [uncertain: exact PageRank personalization multiplier is Aider-specific and may need tuning for Local-Claw]
reference_papers: code2vec: Learning Distributed Representations of Code (Alon et al. 2019) - arxiv:1803.09473 - POPL'19 - represents code as a set of AST paths with path-attention; foundational for AST-path-based symbol/code representation

code2seq: Generating Sequences from Structured Representations of Code (Alon, Brody, Levy, Yahav 2019) - arxiv:1808.01400 - ICLR'19 - encodes compositional AST paths with BiLSTM + attention; basis for AST-aware code summarization/retrieval

RepoGraph: Enhancing AI Software Engineering with Repository-level Code Graph (Ouyang et al. 2024) - arxiv:2410.14684 - builds a repository-level code graph (definitions/references/calls) to give agents holistic cross-file structure for SWE-bench-style tasks

CodexGraph: Bridging Large Language Models and Code Repositories via Code Graph Databases (Liu et al. 2024) - arxiv:2408.03910 - indexes a repo into a graph DB and lets LLM agents query structure (classes-under-module, method-to-definition) precisely; evaluated on CrossCodeEval, SWE-bench, EvoCodeBench

LocAgent: Graph-Guided LLM Agents for Code Localization (Chen et al. 2025) - arxiv:2503.09089 - graph-guided traversal over code structure for code localization, modeling directory/file hierarchy and symbol relations
RANGER: Repository-Level Agent for Graph-Enhanced Retrieval (2025) - arxiv:2509.25257 - graph-centric retrieval encoding definitions/references/calls for repository-level agent reasoning

Tree-sitter: A new parsing system for programming tools (Brunsfeld 2018) - Strange Loop Conference 2018 [uncertain: talk/non-peer-reviewed, no arxiv; primary citation for tree-sitter's incremental, error-tolerant parsing design]

Syntactic Code Search with Sequence-to-Tree Matching / stsearch (Matute, Ni 2024) - UC Berkeley Tech Report EECS-2024-93 - uses tree-sitter error-tolerant parsing to search ASTs (handles files Semgrep cannot parse)
